findings.text: non-blocking: `_attempt_claim_numbers` bounds its scan at `max(pointer attempt, attempt record) + 1` (range(1, highest + 2), line 563) instead of enumerating the directory the way the glob it replaced did, so when two claims are taken without an intervening attempt record — the resume-cut-off-before-spawn window this node exists to read — the newest claim sits two above `highest` and is missed, understating `_current_attempt_number`; the docstring's "Every attempt the run's directory holds a claim for" (line 543) states a coverage the bound does not give.

non-blocking: the same guarded import `from reckon.crew import resumption` and its two-line "cycle" comment are written twice in one module (line 555 and line 592) rather than once; the deferred import is correct because reckon/crew/resumption.py:88 imports this module, but the repetition is a copy that a later edit can leave behind in one place and not the other.

non-blocking: the lint paragraph states "the two changed modules carry 3 findings at the base revision and 3 at the head ... a UP017 among them", but `ruff check` reports one finding (the UP017 at recovery_classification.py:730) at both revisions and the count of 3 is the number of `ruff format --check` hunks in recovery_liveness.py, so the sentence conflates the two tools and describes a UP017 as among the three format hunks; the zero-added-delta conclusion it draws is nonetheless correct.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 0231ca112322d2f02e565eca140525b503a819cc; 56b638531 takes the claim's name from reckon/crew/resumption.py:305, routes the attempt's own end to recovery_liveness.py:628, deletes the duplicated `_attempt_end_recorded` and the re-declared claim-name constants, reverts an out-of-scope import rewrite in recovery_classification.py and the unrelated line joins in recovery_liveness.py, and restates the fixture arms to the exact pane word; dbcb0f06 rewrites the fragment's gate, lint and follow-on paragraphs; all four changed files are inside the declared write paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names four fixture arms, a base arm, a negative control and the ruff/format deltas on tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py; base-gate.log records 5 failed EXIT=1, head-gate.log records 19 passed EXIT=0 over the test plus its two sibling suites, negative-control.log records 4 failed EXIT=1 under the declared mutation, and the ruff figure is a command this review re-ran and confirmed.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to read a resumed attempt's liveness and verdict through its own claim, worker and exit records rather than its predecessor's; the repair round keeps that reading and re-sources it through the modules that own the names, at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:555 (the claim) and reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:84 (the attempt's own end).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, four commits, the single-file gate command on its `tests:` line, four gate logs, baseline_suite at exit 1 with five failure ids and after_suite at exit 0 with none, and follow_ons naming the reducer word for the claim-only arms and the wide sweep that did not complete.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares five paths — the two source modules, the manifest's test, the evidence fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/ and the docs/figures/ directory — and `git diff --stat 0231ca112322d2f02e565eca140525b503a819cc dbcb0f06a72fba273a8cbb8ba8a26a1567fca589` shows exactly the four files those paths name and nothing outside them.

justifications.durability: the four arms fail at the base revision (base-gate.log, 5 failed) and under the declared mutation (negative-control.log, 4 failed), and the repair's exact-word assertion at tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py:286 replaces the membership check that would have accepted any neighbouring working state, so a revert of the claim branch reddens arm i rather than passing quietly.
justifications.evidence: the recorded gate could have failed and did — base-gate.log 5 failed against head-gate.log 19 passed EXIT=0 — and this review re-ran the ruff half of the bare done-when and confirmed the zero delta, but the html's lint paragraph conflates two tool counts (docs/evidence/fragments/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted/a-resumed-attempt-is-read-through-its-own-records.html:29) and its "6 passed in 5.44s" figure has no log named in test_logs, only the widened 19-passed run.
justifications.fit: the additions follow the module's convention of deferred imports and mechanism-stating docstrings (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:553), and no plan label, version or ticket reference appears in an added name or comment, though the deferred import is written twice.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:542 builds each claim path through the owner at reckon/crew/resumption.py:305 instead of re-spelling it, and reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:84 resolves the attempt's end through the single owner at recovery_liveness.py:628, which is the same reading the goal names without the duplicate.
justifications.reuse: the repair resolves the two reuse defects the prior review named — the re-declared claim-file spelling is gone in favour of reckon/crew/resumption.py:305, and `_attempt_end_recorded` is deleted in favour of the existing `_exit_record_names_attempt` at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:628 — with only the bounded scan at recovery_liveness.py:557 a partial fork of the directory enumeration it replaced.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is one the manifest declares and nothing outside them was touched, though the gained diff still carries three line joins in recovery_liveness.py (ruff format hunks at lines 431, 735 and 957) and a two-line import revert in recovery_classification.py that are churn relative to the revision this diff is taken from.
